newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Mideast peace envoy not to have role in talks.
newsitem.headline: EU Mideast peace envoy not to have role in talks.

text.p: A planned special European Union envoy to the Middle East would not be directly involved in peace negotiations, Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Wednesday.
"We do not consider it wise to have another negotiator," Spring told a press conference at the European Parliament.
Ireland is currently the EU president.
EU foreign ministers are due to discuss the plans for an envoy, drawn up by EU leaders at a special summit in Dublin on October 5, when they meet in Luxembourg on Monday.
Spring said it remained to be seen whether the envoy would be a diplomat or a politician.

He sidestepped another question about Israeli hostility to EU, especially French, involvement in the peace process, emphasising that the EU supported the negotiations currently underway involving a United States envoy.
"They are at quite a delicate phase," he said, adding that the EU wanted to see implementation of existing agreements between Israel and the PLO.
Spring said Israeli leaders did not react negatively to the idea of an EU envoy when he visited the Middle East shortly after the Dublin summit.
"It reflects a strong willingness to become actively involved in efforts to revitalise the peace process and build on the major contribution Europe has made over many years to the region," he said.
The EU is the Middle East's main trading partner and the biggest aid donor to the Palestinians.

"A great deal of the prospects for the Middle East peace process depend on the economic regeneration of the Palestinian Authority. I don't see that happening without the active involvement of the EU," he said.
